analysis.title: U.S. Equities Color: Heavy (17 Nov 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -103bps at 7,340, below its 200-day moving average (7,344), with a $2.4bn market-on-close imbalance to sell. NDX -7bps at 27,001, R2K -139bps at 2,703, Dow -164bps at 50,759.
Volume was 18.855bn shares across US exchanges vs a year-to-date daily average of 18.557bn.
Markets sold off after firmer retail sales and intraday headlines about potential cyber incidents. The NSA later clarified that the network outages were linked to software updates.
NVDA reports tonight. The stock was +3% after hours on a better than expected quarter and guide plus an additional $150bn buyback.

Tech focus remains on regulatory proposals: new restrictions on China's access to high-end AI chips (aimed at stopping Chinese firms renting NVDA chips outside the US and getting processors through third countries), a Reuters report that the Trump administration plans to press ahead with blocking imports of Chinese data center equipment, and a new NVDA board committee overseeing national security and export control.
The GS floor rated overall activity 3 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers were net sellers, driven by large cap tech. Hedge fund flows were balanced.
NKE finished -6% (from +3% intraday) on its investor day as investors were deeply skeptical of the 2031 guide. The GS desk was active in the name.
Headline: NVIDIA board chair says the firm does not plan to reinstate Huang.

VIX closed +1061bps at 25.34. Vol and skew were lower early, then jumped on the intraday headlines, with front-end NDX and SPX fixed-strike vols closing up more than 1 vol point. Skew relaxed during the day, and only the belly of the SPX curve closed with a small bid.
GS expects NVDA earnings and VIX expiry to take significant vol premium out of the market before tomorrow's open, relaxing risk parameters as dealer short tails roll off.
The S&P implied move through tomorrow is 1.26%.
